core_conclusion: Boundary orientation creates competition between two stable registry families with opposite directional biases; the equilibrium ground-state crossing reverses the prepared response while its location is strongly edge-model dependent.

provenance.notes: Generated from the current reproducibility release; no illustrative values.

panels.question: Where do the zero-force registry energies cross for the two triangular edge orientations?
Do registry families A and B carry opposite branch-followed directional splittings?
How does selecting the lower-energy prepared registry change the sign across the equilibrium crossing?
How sensitive is the equilibrium crossing angle to outer-site energy weighting?

caption: Figure 4. Boundary-induced competition between registry minima. (a) The zero-force energies of registry families A and B cross at high twist for 20 and 25 deg triangular cuts. (b) The two families carry opposite branch-followed directional splittings. (c) Selecting the lower-energy zero-force state therefore produces a sign reversal of the prepared-state response at the registry switch. (d) Varying the outer-site energy weight shifts the transition substantially, showing that the exact switch angle is edge-model sensitive.
